purpose: Fixed Phase 5 regression benchmark. Reference labels unchanged from the original run.

examples.text: Ray-Ban Meta glasses have a terrible recording light. I returned these smart glasses.

labels.rationale: Criticism and return concern only the smart glasses.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban Meta glasses have a terrible recording light.
I returned these smart glasses.

examples.text: Because of Meta privacy recording scandals, I will never buy Ray-Ban sunglasses again. I distrust the entire Ray-Ban brand now.

labels.rationale: The speaker directly connects the controversy to avoiding traditional sunglasses and distrusting the wider brand.
evidence_quotes: Because of Meta privacy recording scandals, I will never buy Ray-Ban sunglasses again.
I distrust the entire Ray-Ban brand now.

examples.text: Meta is responsible for surveillance. I do not blame Ray-Ban for Meta's decisions.

labels.rationale: Blame is explicitly confined to Meta; Ray-Ban is exonerated.
evidence_quotes: Meta is responsible for surveillance.
I do not blame Ray-Ban for Meta's decisions.

examples.text: I love my traditional Ray-Ban sunglasses. The classic frames look wonderful.

labels.rationale: Traditional eyewear receives praise, without a future purchase statement.
evidence_quotes: I love my traditional Ray-Ban sunglasses.

examples.text: Ray-Ban Meta audio is convenient, but the camera worries me. Ray-Ban's traditional frames still look great.

labels.rationale: The speaker balances convenience against camera concern while praising traditional frames.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban Meta audio is convenient, but the camera worries me.
Ray-Ban's traditional frames still look great.

examples.text: Great, cameras everywhere. Just what we needed. Yeah, right.

labels.rationale: Likely sarcasm about cameras, with no identifiable brand target or spillover evidence.
evidence_quotes: Great, cameras everywhere. Just what we needed. Yeah, right.

examples.text: That changes how I see them. Not sure what I will do.

labels.rationale: The referent and any implications are unspecified.
evidence_quotes: That changes how I see them.

examples.text: The privacy debate is worrying. Ray-Ban's wider brand feels less appealing to me too.

labels.rationale: Privacy concern and diminished wider-brand appeal appear together, without a direct causal statement.
evidence_quotes: The privacy debate is worrying.
Ray-Ban's wider brand feels less appealing to me too.

examples.text: I will buy Ray-Ban Meta glasses because hands-free audio is convenient.

labels.rationale: An explicit product purchase intention is supported by convenience.
evidence_quotes: I will buy Ray-Ban Meta glasses because hands-free audio is convenient.

examples.text: Ray-Ban is responsible for putting cameras in the smart glasses. The recording feature is unsafe.

labels.rationale: Ray-Ban is blamed for a product feature, without rejection of traditional eyewear.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban is responsible for putting cameras in the smart glasses.

examples.text: I won't buy Ray-Ban Meta because its camera records people without consent. My opinion of ordinary Ray-Ban sunglasses is unchanged.

labels.rationale: The purchase rejection concerns the smart glasses; the traditional brand is explicitly unaffected.
evidence_quotes: I won't buy Ray-Ban Meta because its camera records people without consent. My opinion of ordinary Ray-Ban sunglasses is unchanged.

examples.text: Because of Meta's privacy and recording scandals, I will never buy any Ray-Ban frames again.

labels.rationale: The speaker extends rejection from Meta privacy concerns to all Ray-Ban frames.
evidence_quotes: Because of Meta's privacy and recording scandals, I will never buy any Ray-Ban frames again.

examples.text: Meta's privacy scandal made me distrust the entire Ray-Ban brand. I will not buy its traditional sunglasses.

labels.rationale: The text states wider Ray-Ban distrust caused by a Meta privacy controversy and rejects traditional sunglasses.
evidence_quotes: Meta's privacy scandal made me distrust the entire Ray-Ban brand. I will not buy its traditional sunglasses.

examples.text: I blame Meta, not Ray-Ban, for its data collection. I still trust Ray-Ban sunglasses.

labels.rationale: Meta receives blame while the traditional Ray-Ban brand retains trust; no purchase intention is stated.
evidence_quotes: I blame Meta, not Ray-Ban, for its data collection. I still trust Ray-Ban sunglasses.

examples.text: The recording indicator reassures me. I will buy Ray-Ban Meta for hands-free calls.

labels.rationale: The speaker praises a recording safeguard and explicitly intends to buy the product.
evidence_quotes: The recording indicator reassures me. I will buy Ray-Ban Meta for hands-free calls.

examples.text: The smart-glasses privacy debate worries me. Ray-Ban's ordinary sunglasses feel less appealing now.

labels.rationale: Privacy concern co-occurs with lower traditional-brand appeal, without an explicit causal statement.
evidence_quotes: The smart-glasses privacy debate worries me. Ray-Ban's ordinary sunglasses feel less appealing now.

examples.text: Their choices changed everything. I might reconsider.

labels.rationale: Neither the referent, emotional direction nor purchase decision is specified.
evidence_quotes: Their choices changed everything. I might reconsider.

examples.text: Sure, Ray-Ban Meta recording strangers is a brilliant idea. /s

labels.rationale: Sarcasm indicates criticism of the product; the statement does not establish wider-brand consequences.
evidence_quotes: Sure, Ray-Ban Meta recording strangers is a brilliant idea. /s

examples.text: My Ray-Ban sunglasses are stylish. Meta's surveillance worries me, but I will buy more traditional Ray-Ban frames.

labels.rationale: The speaker criticizes Meta surveillance but retains positive traditional-brand sentiment and purchase intent.
evidence_quotes: My Ray-Ban sunglasses are stylish. Meta's surveillance worries me, but I will buy more traditional Ray-Ban frames.

examples.text: The Meta privacy controversy is why I refuse to purchase any traditional Ray-Ban eyewear.

labels.rationale: A direct causal statement links a privacy controversy to rejection of traditional Ray-Ban eyewear.
evidence_quotes: The Meta privacy controversy is why I refuse to purchase any traditional Ray-Ban eyewear.
